name: Canglang Washing Body Canon (Thương Lãng Trạc Thể Kinh)
concept: The founder's method, named for the old song: when the Canglang water is clear, wash your hat strings; when it is muddy, wash your feet. The disciple tempers the body in the frost sea, one dive deeper for each layer, and learns to take what the water gives: clear water washes the qi, muddy water hardens the skin. It runs on no element, so any fisher's child with good bones can learn it. In a fight it is endurance: health that rises when struck by cold or water, a grip that does not let go, and lungs that outlast the foe.
lore: Khuất Thanh Anh made it in 830 from the way the frost-coast seal hunters had always trained their sons: into the sea in winter, and out again before the heart stops.

name: Whale-Line Harpoon Rite (Kình Tác Lao Pháp)
concept: The sea hunters' harpoon art: a thrown iron on a qi-woven line that binds the foe (it cannot flee), then makes its soonest art wait 0.3 s. The hunter fights tethered to the foe and finishes with the body canon's grip. It is a force art and takes no element, only a strong back.
lore: Taught only on the terrace, with the line made from the founder's whale sinew, which has not frayed in 370 years.
